name: Spinning Top
description: A single candle with a small real body and relatively long upper and lower wicks of roughly equal length. Indicates indecision in the market where neither buyers nor sellers gained a significant advantage during the session. Similar to a doji but with a more visible real body.

body_rules.body_size: small but visible; larger than a doji body but still small relative to total range
body_rules.body_color: either bullish or bearish; color is not relevant to the pattern
body_rules.body_to_range_ratio: body typically accounts for 10-30% of the total candle range

wick_rules.upper_wick: long; at least equal to or longer than the real body
wick_rules.lower_wick: long; at least equal to or longer than the real body
wick_rules.symmetry: upper and lower wicks should be of similar length; asymmetric wicks shift it toward hammer or shooting star territory

context_requirement: most meaningful at the top of an uptrend (potential reversal) or bottom of a downtrend (potential reversal); in consolidation it confirms ongoing indecision without adding new information
volume_requirement: volume is secondary; very high volume spinning top at a key level adds weight to the indecision signal — neither side could win decisively despite heavy participation
agent_rules: Never trade a spinning top in isolation; always require a following directional candle for confirmation
At resistance after an uptrend: treat as a potential bearish reversal signal; wait for bearish confirmation candle
At support after a downtrend: treat as a potential bullish reversal signal; wait for bullish confirmation candle
A cluster of spinning tops indicates a consolidation zone; wait for a breakout candle
High volume spinning top at a key level is more significant than a low volume one
Spinning top is less significant than a doji at the same location due to its visible body
